chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Isa ibn Abdullah, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon him)
that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did not reject the perfume and the sweets.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet do when offered perfume and sweets?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in al-Kafi, illustrates the Prophet Muhammad’s (peace be upon him and his family) gentle etiquette (adab) by accepting gifts of perfume and sweets without refusal, thereby establishing a normative practice of graciousness in social interactions. In Shia scholarly tradition, this is often interpreted not merely as politeness but as an affirmation of the value of sensory pleasures (laza'ij) within the bounds of propriety, countering excessive asceticism. It serves as a practical guideline for maintaining social bonds through the acceptance of gifts, reflecting the Prophet’s approachable nature.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Hilal, from Isa Bin Abdullah, from his father, from his grandfather,
(It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> that: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> never used to reject the perfume and the sweets’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Hilal from ‘Isa ibn ‘Abd Allah from his father from his grandfather who has said the following:
“The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, would not refuse to accept perfume and sweet (fruit).”’
